chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the saying of God, the Exalted: 'And to complete the period.' He said: 'Thirty days.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the sixth Imam
key_terms.العِدَّة: The prescribed waiting period (usually for divorce or death)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'to complete the period' refer to in terms of duration?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the Quranic phrase 'to complete the period' (lit. 'to complete the number/count') as thirty days, likely referring to the waiting period (iddah) for widows or the duration of specific ritual states. This juristic explanation underscores the Imams' role in elucidating precise legal details embedded within Quranic verses, reinforcing the Shia tradition of deriving specific rulings from the Prophet's household. The identification of 'thirty' as the complete count highlights the significance of numerical precision in Islamic jurisprudence.
